slot.brief: Given limiting molar conductivities of a strong acid, its sodium salt and sodium hydroxide, calculate Λ°m of the weak acid by linear combination.

stem: At $298\ \text{K}$, $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})=426$, $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})=91$ and $\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})=126$, all in $\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$. Find $\Lambda_m^\circ$ for acetic acid.

verdicts.working: By Kohlrausch’s law, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 426 + 91 − 126 = 391 S cm² mol⁻¹.

working:
$\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})$
$=426+91-126=391\ \text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$

Independent check: By Kohlrausch’s law, Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(HCl) + Λ°(CH₃COONa) − Λ°(NaCl) = 426 + 91 − 126 = 391 S cm² mol⁻¹.
solution:
By Kohlrausch’s law of independent ionic migration,
$$\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{CH_3COOH})=\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{HCl})+\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{CH_3COONa})-\Lambda_m^\circ(\mathrm{NaCl})$$
$=426+91-126=391\ \mathrm{S\ cm^2\ mol^{-1}}$.
